commits.summary: style_records: the 113-byte Music Stylist parameter block (not 115) is decoded from its three maincpu readers (EffectMode_UpdateBitFlags plus the 30-entry table WidgetStyleDataTable_0x2A8 at 0xEB7BDA, which is the same in v7/v9/v10; BitMapOut_ByteData_PatchTable; EffectMode_CopyVoiceParams). Each record now has one row per panel field and a two-line header. The tempo matches the display string in 991 of 1000 records.
tone_database_directory: each of the 25 tone-number banks and the coefficient bank map now names its subcpu reader and the formula it uses.

tone_database_aux: zone records are typed rows (new data macros); key maps point at their curve by label; the 26 drum kits are decoded to show which instrument each note plays (cross-checked against the separate name path); the 610 PercInst records have headers taken from the code that reads them; the drawbar blobs were never 'segment lists' and are now shown to be 9*9*9 zone records.

tone_database_records: the old 'layer configuration' is split into the part-mode byte, the partial mask and +0x12..+0x14. Each block says which partial it serves, each 81-byte partial block is cut into its 7 field groups (defined by the code that reads them), and each record has a header saying which bank/program selects it. Three old claims are corrected (the old text is kept and marked).

tone_database_aux: fixes this lane's own claim that PercInst layer bytes +0x03/+0x04 and +0x0F..+0x14 have no reader. They are read as tune (Voice_Pitch_CopyBase) and as the drum-voice filter (TVF_BuildEmit_Short_Dispatch and related routines).
tone_database_aux: the 487 SET descriptors are now one ToneSetDesc row each. The header also records how the search for readers of +0x0E and flag bit 3 was done.

tone_database_records: +0x13 is the bend type (Voice_Pitch_Compute_Inactive). The list of routines known to read the common block grows from 3 to 9, including the octave shift, algorithm type, level offset and secondary parameters.
style_records: part 03 is 'PART 4' in the part-name table at 0xE9F374; which panel part that is on the instrument is not established.

tone_database_records: each record's common block is cut into 10 groups defined by the code that reads it. The bytes at +0x2B..+0x5A form twelve 4-byte entries; this is measured from the data and marked as such.

tone_database_aux: DrawbarPreset_Jazz/Rock (tone numbers 336/337, part mode 0x40) now use the same field layout as the other tone records, with 4 partial blocks mapped directly (no packing). Also fixes the object-boundary rule in the tool.

tone_database: the 'MixerDefaultTable' and 'PercMixerDefaultTable' are velocity-split records, not mixer defaults: 3 velocity thresholds, then 4 {wave, family} pairs, one per velocity zone (Velocity_Select_Split_Zone 0x022824, WaveSel_StageA2_FromVelZone 0x0328B5). The descriptions of ToneIndexMapA/B and PercSourceIndexMapA, which index these tables, are corrected. ToneDB_DefaultLayerParams is confirmed as the block used when a partial is absent.

tone_database_aux: renamed the 974 SET chunks ToneEnv_RecNNN_A/_B to ToneSet_NNN_KeyMap/_Zones with a committed sed script (scripts/renaming/rename_tonedb_set_chunks.sed). The chunks contain no envelope data.
notes/tonedb-2026-09-25/README.md: brought in line with the rename (notes only).

leads:
1. **The subcpu's InterCPU_E1_DMA_Transfer header probably has source and destination swapped.**
   - It says XWA is the main-CPU destination.
   - But DSP_Reinit_VoiceSlots passes XWA=0x007800, which is its own staging image (DSP_ResetWriteBufferPtr sets (0x04531C)=0x7800), and XDE=0x1E0000.
   - The maincpu restores the same 0x72AA bytes from its SRAM at 0x1E0000 to subcpu 0x7800.
   - This is for the subcpu lane.
2. **Many subcpu comments say "tonerec+NN" for the pointer at voice slot +0x23, which is the part record (0x041368+part*0x11F), not the tone record.**
   - The tone record is at slot +0x13; paramA (the partial block or PercInst layer) is at +0x17.
   - Many of those offsets are part-record fields.
3. **analysis/disk-format-probes/README-lsw-part-record-fields.md calls the style parameter block a "DSP-effect preset".** It is the Music Stylist record: CopyVoiceParams byte 31 is style-record byte +0x6C.
4. **Each style's DSP effect could be named.**
   - EffEdit_ValidateAndReadParams reads parameter id 0x4900 (& 0x7F) into RAM 0x2976.
   - DspItem0_DisplayEffectName uses 0x2976 to index DspEffectName_PtrTable.
   - If DSPCfg_ReadParam_Map0(0x4900) resolves to tag 0x61 +0 (style record +0x9E), every one of the 1000 styles gets a named effect.
5. **Wave-selection chain, now complete from the code (worth a technics-docs page for MAME/HLE):**
   - partial block +0x02 wave / +0x03 family
   - -> StageA1 index map (dir +0x0C/+0x10/+0x14)
   - -> velocity-split record (dir +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, 11 bytes)
   - -> velocity zone -> {wave, family}
   - -> StageA2 map (dir +0x24/+0x28/+0x2C)
   - -> SET descriptor
   - -> key map -> zone record
   - -> TG register +0x040 selector
6. **WSA1 prom_d has the same directory slots** (+0x18/+0x20 are 43-byte 'wave-select' records there). The velocity-split reading (3 thresholds + {wave, family} pairs per zone) is a candidate framing to test against prom_c's readers.
7. **Tone records +0x2B..+0x5A are twelve 4-byte entries in three runs of four.** Only entries 0-3 have a reader (ExtVoice_Build_SlotRegisters, selected by voice +0x1A & 3). The other two runs are likely per-partial parameter sets; look for readers that index +0x3B+4k or +0x4B+4k.
8. **Bank-0x40 drum kits do not follow the GM note layout; kits 14-17/19/20 (selector 0x41) do.** A MAME/HLE drum map should use the ROM's per-kit note table, not GM.
9. **Regenerate symbols/table_data_symbols_reference.txt** (the ToneSet_* rename).
